The lan8814 represents a package of 4 PHYs. All of them are sharing the
same interrupt line. So when a link was going down/up or a frame was
timestamped
column2: then the interrupt handler of all the PHYs was called.

column1: Which is all fine and expected but the problem is the way the handler
interrupt works.
Basically if one of the PHYs timestamp a frame
PHYs were polling the status of the interrupt until that PHY actually
cleared the interrupt by reading the timestamp.
The reason of polling was in case another PHY was also timestamping a
frame at the same time
column2: it could miss this interrupt. But this is not

column1: the right approach
column2: because it is the interrupt controller who needs to

column1: call the interrupt handlers again if the interrupt line is still
active.
Therefore change this such when the interrupt handler is called check
only if the interrupt is for itself
column2: otherwise just exit. In this way

column1: save CPU usage.
